title: tcpdump on the server and reading the pcap file

videos.script: The server is where the problem is, and the server has no screen. {{server}} It does have tcpdump. It speaks the same capture filters as Wireshark, and it prints one line per packet. {{line}} Each line says who sent what to whom. The time, two addresses with their ports, the TCP flags, the sequence numbers, the length. Read four of them in a row and you can see a connection open. {{flags}} Reading lines as they scroll past only works for a handful of packets. So tcpdump writes a file instead. {{file}} You will write one, give it away from root, and describe it with capinfos. Then you will read it back with filters. {{read}} Two flags keep a capture in bounds. The snap length keeps only the start of each packet. A ring of files keeps only the last few megabytes, so a capture can run all night. {{ring}} And then the file leaves the server. It holds everything that crossed the wire, so the last thing this lesson covers is how little to keep, and when to delete it. {{privacy}}
